key_insight: Multimodal LLMs can be repurposed for audio deepfake detection by combining raw audio (or audio embeddings) with targeted text prompts, yielding promising cross-modal representations while revealing modality-specific adaptation needs.
problem_solved: Addresses the unexplored challenge of whether Vision/Multimodal Large Language Models can detect audio deepfakes—reducing reliance on bespoke audio-only detectors and testing if MLLMs generalise to audio-domain manipulation detection.
method: Convert audio to model-compatible inputs (waveform embeddings, spectrograms or pretrained audio embeddings) and feed them into MLLMs alongside designed text prompts.
Use prompt engineering and prompt-as-query strategies to probe MLLMs for deepfake indicators and extract multimodal representations.
Evaluate detection performance across prompt types and baselines (audio-only detectors), analyze failure modes and modality-alignment issues.
impact: Demonstrates a pathway to unified, multimodal deepfake detectors and highlights practical considerations (prompt design, modality alignment, fine-tuning) for deploying MLLMs in audio security tasks—helpful for practitioners seeking robust, scalable detection systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: audio -> embedding/spectrogram -> MLLM + text prompt -> detection score
Bar/line chart comparing detection performance across prompt types and baselines (audio-only vs. MLLM)
Attention/activation overlay on spectrogram showing which audio regions the MLLM attends to
Failure-mode matrix or ROC curves illustrating trade-offs and where MLLMs succeed or struggle
paper_title: Investigating the Viability of Employing Multi-modal Large Language Models in the Context of Audio Deepfake Detection
paper_authors: Akanksha Chuchra, Shukesh Reddy, Sudeepta Mishra, Abhijit Das, Abhinav Dhall
